## 17. At work: meeting a colleague (Un nouveau collègue) · B1

*Scene:* It's Mehdi's first day in a new office. Aurélie, his team lead, welcomes him, tells him that everyone uses tu here and introduces two colleagues. Then she plans to explain his first project.

Speakers: **Aurélie**, team lead · **Mehdi**, new colleague

| Speaker | French | Pronunciation | English |
|---|---|---|---|
| Aurélie | Bonjour ! Tu es Mehdi ? Moi, c'est Aurélie, je suis responsable de l'équipe. | bohN-zhoor. tew eh meh-dee. mwah, seh oh-ray-lee, zhuh swee reh-spohN-sahbl duh lay-keep | Hello! Are you Mehdi? I'm Aurélie, I'm the team lead. |
| Mehdi | Oui, bonjour ! Enchanté. Je commence aujourd'hui. | wee, bohN-zhoor. ahN-shahN-tay. zhuh koh-mahNs oh-zhoor-dwee | Yes, hello! Nice to meet you. I'm starting today. |
| Aurélie | Bienvenue ! Ici, tout le monde se tutoie. Ça te va ? | byaN-vuh-new. ee-see, too luh mohNd suh tew-twah. sah tuh vah | Welcome! Everyone says tu to each other here. Is that OK with you? |
| Mehdi | Oui, pas de problème. Tu peux me montrer mon bureau ? | wee, pah duh proh-blem. tew puh muh mohN-tray mohN bew-roh | Yes, no problem. Can you show me my desk? |
| Aurélie | Bien sûr, viens. Voici Paul. C'est notre développeur. | byaN sewr, vyaN. vwah-see pohl. seh noh-truh day-vuh-loh-puhr | Of course, come with me. This is Paul. He's our developer. |
| Mehdi | Il a l'air sympa. Il travaille ici depuis longtemps ? | eel ah lair saN-pah. eel trah-vahy ee-see duh-pwee lohN-tahN | He seems nice. Has he been working here long? |
| Aurélie | Oui, il est très sympa. En fait, il est là depuis cinq ans. | wee, eel eh treh saN-pah. ahN fet, eel eh lah duh-pwee saN kahN | Yes, he's very nice. Actually, he's been here for five years. |
| Mehdi | Et la femme à côté de la fenêtre, c'est qui ? | ay lah fahm ah koh-tay duh lah fuh-neh-truh, seh kee | And the woman next to the window, who's that? |
| Aurélie | C'est Sarah. Elle est ingénieure, elle vient de Lyon. | seh sah-rah. el eh aN-zhay-nyuhr, el vyaN duh lee-ohN | That's Sarah. She's an engineer; she's from Lyon. |
| Mehdi | Moi aussi, je viens de Lyon ! Je vais lui dire bonjour. | mwah oh-see, zhuh vyaN duh lee-ohN. zhuh veh lwee deer bohN-zhoor | I'm from Lyon too! I'll go and say hello to her. |
| Aurélie | Bonne idée. Après, je t'explique ton premier projet. | bun ee-day. ah-preh, zhuh tek-spleek tohN pruh-myay proh-zheh | Good idea. Afterwards, I'll explain your first project to you. |
| Mehdi | Ça marche. À tout à l'heure, et merci pour ton aide ! | sah marsh. ah too‿tah luhr, ay mair-see poor tohN‿ned | Sounds good. See you in a bit, and thanks for your help! |

### Key vocabulary

| French | Pronunciation | English | See |
|---|---|---|---|
| Enchanté | ahN-shahN-tay | Nice to meet you (a woman says enchantée) | *Enchanté(e)* |
| Je commence | zhuh koh-mahNs | I'm starting | *commencer* |
| Tu peux me montrer | tew puh muh mohN-tray | Can you show me | *montrer* |
| il travaille ici | eel trah-vahy ee-see | he works here | *travailler* |
| en fait | ahN fet | actually, in fact | *en fait* |
| Elle est ingénieure | el eh aN-zhay-nyuhr | She's an engineer (no article before a job after elle est) | Grammar tables: C'est or il est? |
| elle vient de Lyon | el vyaN duh lee-ohN | she's from Lyon (de + city) | Grammar tables: Cities and countries: à, en, au, aux |
| Je vais lui dire bonjour | zhuh veh lwee deer bohN-zhoor | I'll go and say hello to her (lui: to her / to him) | Grammar tables: Indirect object pronouns: me, lui, leur... |
| je t'explique | zhuh tek-spleek | I'll explain to you | *expliquer* |
| À tout à l'heure | ah too‿tah luhr | See you later (the same day) | *À tout à l'heure* |

### Notice this: C'est or il est?

Aurélie uses c'est + a name or a noun with a determiner: C'est Paul. C'est notre développeur. To describe someone with an adjective or a bare job, she uses il est / elle est: Il est très sympa. Elle est ingénieure. After il est / elle est, a job takes no article.

- **C'est notre développeur.** (seh noh-truh day-vuh-loh-puhr) — *He's our developer. (c'est + determiner + noun)*
- **Elle est ingénieure.** (el eh aN-zhay-nyuhr) — *She's an engineer. (elle est + job, no article)*
- **Il est très sympa.** (eel eh treh saN-pah) — *He's very nice. (il est + adjective)*

See the table: Grammar tables, C'est or il est?

### Comprehension questions

1. What is Aurélie's job?
   a) Developer
   b) Engineer
   c) Receptionist
   d) Team lead
2. How long has Paul worked there?
   a) Five years
   b) Six months
   c) Ten years
   d) Two years
3. Where is Sarah from?
   a) Lille
   b) Lyon
   c) Marseille
   d) Paris
4. How does Aurélie say that everyone uses tu?
   a) Ici, personne ne se tutoie.
   b) Ici, tout le monde se dit bonjour.
   c) Ici, tout le monde se tutoie.
   d) Ici, tout le monde se vouvoie.

## 18. Renting a flat (Louer un appartement) · B1

*Scene:* Laura is looking for a flat and visits a small one with the landlord, M. Girard. He shows her the bright living room and the quiet bedroom, and tells her about the area, the rent and the deposit. Laura wants to think it over before she decides.

Speakers: **M. Girard**, landlord · **Laura**, prospective tenant

| Speaker | French | Pronunciation | English |
|---|---|---|---|
| M. Girard | Bonjour, madame. Entrez, je vous en prie. | bohN-zhoor, mah-dahm. ahN-tray, zhuh voo‿zahN pree | Hello. Come in, please. |
| Laura | Merci. C'est l'appartement que j'ai vu sur Internet ? | mair-see. seh lah-par-tuh-mahN kuh zhay vew sewr aN-tair-net | Thank you. Is this the flat I saw online? (US: apartment) |
| M. Girard | Oui, c'est bien ça : deux pièces, quarante mètres carrés. | wee, seh byaN sah. duh pyes, kah-rahNt meh-truh kah-ray | Yes, that's right: two rooms, forty square metres. (a living room and one bedroom) |
| Laura | Il est clair ! Et la chambre, elle est où ? | eel eh klair. ay lah shahN-bruh, el eh oo | It's bright! And the bedroom, where is it? |
| M. Girard | Ici, à gauche. C'est la chambre qui donne sur la cour, donc elle est très calme. | ee-see, ah gohsh. seh lah shahN-bruh kee dun sewr lah koor, dohNk el eh treh kahlm | Here, on the left. It's the bedroom that looks onto the courtyard, so it's very quiet. |
| Laura | Ça me plaît. Il y a une boulangerie près d'ici ? | sah muh pleh. eel ee ah ewn boo-lahN-zhuh-ree preh dee-see | I like it. Is there a bakery near here? |
| M. Girard | Oui, juste en face. C'est le quartier où j'habite, il est très vivant. | wee, zhewst ahN fahs. seh luh kar-tyay oo zhah-beet, eel eh treh vee-vahN | Yes, just opposite. It's the area where I live; it's very lively. (US: neighborhood) |
| Laura | Et le loyer, c'est combien par mois ? | ay luh lwah-yay, seh kohN-byaN par mwah | And the rent, how much is it a month? |
| M. Girard | Huit cent cinquante euros, plus cinquante euros de charges. | wee sahN saN-kahN tuh-roh, plews saN-kahN tuh-roh duh sharzh | Eight hundred and fifty euros, plus fifty euros for service charges. |
| Laura | C'est quand même cher. Il faut payer une caution ? | seh kahN mem shair. eel foh peh-yay ewn koh-syohN | That's quite expensive, though. Do I have to pay a deposit? |
| M. Girard | Oui, un mois de loyer. L'appartement est libre le premier mars. | wee, uhN mwah duh lwah-yay. lah-par-tuh-mahN eh lee-bruh luh pruh-myay mars | Yes, one month's rent. The flat is free from the first of March. |
| Laura | D'accord. Je vais réfléchir et je vous rappelle demain. | dah-kor. zhuh veh ray-flay-sheer ay zhuh voo rah-pel duh-maN | OK. I'll think it over and call you back tomorrow. |
| M. Girard | Très bien. Voici mon numéro. Au revoir, madame. | treh byaN. vwah-see mohN new-may-roh. oh ruh-vwahr, mah-dahm | Very good. Here's my number. Goodbye. |

### Key vocabulary

| French | Pronunciation | English | See |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entrez | ahN-tray | Come in (polite) | *entrer* |
| l'appartement que j'ai vu | lah-par-tuh-mahN kuh zhay vew | the flat (that) I saw | *voir* |
| quarante mètres carrés | kah-rahNt meh-truh kah-ray | forty square metres (40 m²) | Grammar tables: Numbers 21–100 |
| la chambre qui donne sur la cour | lah shahN-bruh kee dun sewr lah koor | the bedroom that looks onto the courtyard (qui: subject) | Grammar tables: Relative pronouns: qui, que, où, dont |
| Ça me plaît | sah muh pleh | I like it (literally: it pleases me) | *Ça me plaît* |
| Il y a une boulangerie près d'ici ? | eel ee ah ewn boo-lahN-zhuh-ree preh dee-see | Is there a bakery near here? | *Il y a … près d'ici ?* |
| juste en face | zhewst ahN fahs | just opposite (US: right across the street) | Grammar tables: Prepositions of place |
| le quartier où j'habite | luh kar-tyay oo zhah-beet | the area where I live (où: place) | *habiter* |
| quand même | kahN mem | all the same, though | *quand même* |
| Je vais réfléchir | zhuh veh ray-flay-sheer | I'll think it over | *réfléchir* |

### Notice this: Qui, que, où: joining two ideas

M. Girard and Laura join two ideas with a relative pronoun: la chambre qui donne sur la cour (qui is the subject of the next verb), l'appartement que j'ai vu (que is the object; a new subject follows) and le quartier où j'habite (où for a place). English can drop 'that', but French never drops que.

- **C'est la chambre qui donne sur la cour.** (seh lah shahN-bruh kee dun sewr lah koor) — *It's the bedroom that looks onto the courtyard. (qui + verb)*
- **C'est l'appartement que j'ai vu.** (seh lah-par-tuh-mahN kuh zhay vew) — *It's the flat (that) I saw. (que + subject + verb)*
- **C'est le quartier où j'habite.** (seh luh kar-tyay oo zhah-beet) — *It's the area where I live. (où: a place)*

See the table: Grammar tables, Relative pronouns: qui, que, où, dont.

### Comprehension questions

1. How big is the flat?
   a) Fifty square metres
   b) Forty square metres
   c) Forty-four square metres
   d) Fourteen square metres
2. What does the bedroom look onto?
   a) A park
   b) The courtyard
   c) The station
   d) The street
3. How much is the rent, without charges?
   a) €580 a month
   b) €800 a month
   c) €850 a month
   d) €900 a month
4. What does Laura say at the end?
   a) Je le prends tout de suite.
   b) Je ne veux pas l'appartement.
   c) Je vais réfléchir et je vous rappelle demain.
   d) Je vais signer aujourd'hui.

## 19. A small complaint (Une réclamation au magasin) · B1

*Scene:* Nadia brings back a kettle she bought last week, because it has stopped working. Thierry, the shop manager, checks her receipt and offers to send it for repair. Nadia politely asks for an exchange or a refund, and they agree on an exchange.

Speakers: **Nadia**, customer · **Thierry**, shop manager

| Speaker | French | Pronunciation | English |
|---|---|---|---|
| Nadia | Bonjour, monsieur. Excusez-moi, je voudrais voir le responsable. | bohN-zhoor, muh-syuh. eks-kew-zay mwah, zhuh voo-dreh vwahr luh reh-spohN-sahbl | Hello. Excuse me, I'd like to see the manager. |
| Thierry | C'est moi. Qu'est-ce que je peux faire pour vous ? | seh mwah. kes-kuh zhuh puh fair poor voo | That's me. What can I do for you? |
| Nadia | J'ai acheté cette bouilloire la semaine dernière, et elle ne marche plus. | zhay ahsh-tay set boo-ywahr lah suh-men dair-nyair, ay el nuh marsh plew | I bought this kettle last week, and it doesn't work any more. |
| Thierry | Je suis désolé, madame. Vous avez le ticket de caisse ? | zhuh swee day-zoh-lay, mah-dahm. voo‿zah-vay luh tee-keh duh kes | I'm sorry, madam. Do you have the receipt? |
| Nadia | Oui, le voilà. Je n'ai rien fait de spécial, je l'ai juste utilisée deux fois. | wee, luh vwah-lah. zhuh nay ryaN feh duh spay-syahl, zhuh lay zhewst ew-tee-lee-zay duh fwah | Yes, here it is. I didn't do anything unusual; I've only used it twice. |
| Thierry | Nous pouvons l'envoyer en réparation, si vous voulez. | noo poo-vohN lahN-vwah-yay ahN ray-pah-rah-syohN, see voo voo-lay | We can send it off for repair, if you like. |
| Nadia | Ça prendrait combien de temps ? | sah prahN-dreh kohN-byaN duh tahN | How long would that take? |
| Thierry | Trois semaines, à peu près. | trwah suh-men, ah puh preh | About three weeks. |
| Nadia | C'est assez long. Pourriez-vous plutôt me l'échanger ou me rembourser ? | seh‿tah-seh lohN. poo-ryay voo plew-toh muh lay-shahN-zhay oo muh rahN-boor-say | That's rather long. Could you exchange it or give me a refund instead? |
| Thierry | Je ne peux pas vous rendre l'argent, mais je peux vous l'échanger. | zhuh nuh puh pah voo rahN-druh lar-zhahN, meh zhuh puh voo lay-shahN-zhay | I can't give you your money back, but I can exchange it for you. |
| Nadia | D'accord. Je voudrais le même modèle, s'il vous plaît. | dah-kor. zhuh voo-dreh luh mem moh-del, seel voo pleh | OK. I'd like the same model, please. |
| Thierry | Bien sûr. Attendez un instant, je vais la chercher en réserve. | byaN sewr. ah-tahN-day uhN‿naN-stahN, zhuh veh lah shair-shay ahN ray-zairv | Of course. Wait a moment; I'll fetch one from the stockroom. |
| Nadia | Merci beaucoup, c'est très gentil. | mair-see boh-koo, seh treh zhahN-tee | Thank you very much, that's very kind. |

### Key vocabulary

| French | Pronunciation | English | See |
|---|---|---|---|
| Excusez-moi | eks-kew-zay mwah | Excuse me | *Excusez-moi* |
| je voudrais voir le responsable | zhuh voo-dreh vwahr luh reh-spohN-sahbl | I'd like to see the manager (je voudrais: polite conditional) | *Je voudrais…* |
| J'ai acheté | zhay ahsh-tay | I bought | *acheter* |
| elle ne marche plus | el nuh marsh plew | it doesn't work any more (ne… plus) | *marcher* |
| Je suis désolé | zhuh swee day-zoh-lay | I'm sorry (a woman says désolée) | *Je suis désolé(e)* |
| Je n'ai rien fait | zhuh nay ryaN feh | I didn't do anything (ne… rien) | Grammar tables: Negative words |
| Pourriez-vous | poo-ryay voo | Could you…? (polite conditional of pouvoir) | *pouvoir* |
| me l'échanger | muh lay-shahN-zhay | exchange it for me (l' = la bouilloire) | Grammar tables: Direct object pronouns: me, le, la... |
| vous rendre l'argent | voo rahN-druh lar-zhahN | give you your money back | *rendre* |
| Attendez un instant | ah-tahN-day uhN‿naN-stahN | Wait a moment (polite) | *attendre* |

### Notice this: Ne… plus, ne… rien: negative words

Nadia says Elle ne marche plus (it doesn't work any more) and Je n'ai rien fait (I didn't do anything). Like ne… pas, the two parts go around the verb, or around avoir in the passé composé. Ne… jamais (never) works the same way: Je ne l'ai jamais utilisée.

- **Elle ne marche plus.** (el nuh marsh plew) — *It doesn't work any more. (ne… plus)*
- **Je n'ai rien fait.** (zhuh nay ryaN feh) — *I didn't do anything. (ne… rien)*
- **Je ne l'ai jamais utilisée.** (zhuh nuh lay zhah-meh ew-tee-lee-zay) — *I've never used it. (ne… jamais)*

See the table: Grammar tables, Negative words.

### Comprehension questions

1. What is wrong with Nadia's kettle?
   a) It doesn't work any more
   b) It leaks
   c) It's the wrong colour
   d) It's too small
2. How long would a repair take?
   a) About a month
   b) About three days
   c) About three weeks
   d) About two weeks
3. What does Thierry agree to do?
   a) Exchange the kettle
   b) Give her a discount
   c) Give her a refund
   d) Send it for repair
4. How does Nadia politely ask for an exchange or a refund?
   a) Je voudrais voir le responsable.
   b) Pourriez-vous l'envoyer en réparation ?
   c) Pourriez-vous plutôt me l'échanger ou me rembourser ?
   d) Vous devez me rembourser tout de suite.

## 20. Hobbies and free time (Les loisirs) · B1

*Scene:* Zoé and her friend Bastien are chatting about what they do in their free time. She runs and loves reading; he plays football and is learning the guitar. They share their opinions and make a plan for Sunday.

Speakers: **Zoé**, friend · **Bastien**, friend

| Speaker | French | Pronunciation | English |
|---|---|---|---|
| Zoé | Alors, qu'est-ce que tu fais pendant ton temps libre ? | ah-lor, kes-kuh tew feh pahN-dahN tohN tahN lee-bruh | So, what do you do in your free time? |
| Bastien | Je joue au foot le samedi, et en fait, j'apprends la guitare. | zhuh zhoo oh foot luh sahm-dee, ay ahN fet, zhah-prahN lah gee-tar | I play football on Saturdays, and actually, I'm learning the guitar. (US: soccer) |
| Zoé | C'est génial ! Moi, j'adore la lecture et je cours trois fois par semaine. | seh zhay-nyahl. mwah, zhah-dor lah lek-tewr ay zhuh koor trwah fwah par suh-men | That's great! As for me, I love reading and I run three times a week. |
| Bastien | Trois fois ? Moi, j'ai souvent la flemme de faire du sport après le travail. | trwah fwah. mwah, zhay soo-vahN lah flem duh fair dew spor ah-preh luh trah-vahy | Three times? I often can't be bothered to do sport after work. (US: sports) |
| Zoé | Je pense que courir, c'est le meilleur moyen de se détendre. | zhuh pahNs kuh koo-reer, seh luh meh-yuhr mwah-yaN duh suh day-tahN-druh | I think running is the best way to relax. |
| Bastien | Peut-être, mais je déteste courir. Je préfère les sports d'équipe. | puh-teh-truh, meh zhuh day-test koo-reer. zhuh pray-fair lay spor day-keep | Maybe, but I hate running. I prefer team sports. |
| Zoé | Et la guitare, ça te plaît ? | ay lah gee-tar, sah tuh pleh | And the guitar, do you like it? |
| Bastien | Oui, beaucoup ! C'est difficile, mais je fais quand même des progrès. | wee, boh-koo. seh dee-fee-seel, meh zhuh feh kahN mem day proh-greh | Yes, a lot! It's hard, but I'm making progress all the same. |
| Zoé | Du coup, tu pourrais me jouer quelque chose un jour ? | dew koo, tew poo-reh muh zhoo-ay kel-kuh shohz uhN zhoor | So, could you play me something one day? |
| Bastien | D'accord, mais alors, tu m'emmènes courir dimanche. | dah-kor, meh ah-lor, tew mahN-men koo-reer dee-mahNsh | OK, but then you're taking me running on Sunday. |
| Zoé | Ça marche ! Mais je cours vite, tu sais. | sah marsh. meh zhuh koor veet, tew seh | Deal! But I run fast, you know. |
| Bastien | Pas de problème. Bref, dimanche, on court, et après, on va boire un verre ! | pah duh proh-blem. bref, dee-mahNsh, ohN koor, ay ah-preh, ohN vah bwahr uhN vair | No problem. Anyway, on Sunday we run, and afterwards we go for a drink! |

### Key vocabulary

| French | Pronunciation | English | See |
|---|---|---|---|
| Alors | ah-lor | so, well (to start or move a conversation on) | *alors* |
| Je joue au foot | zhuh zhoo oh foot | I play football (jouer à + le = au) | *jouer* |
| j'apprends la guitare | zhah-prahN lah gee-tar | I'm learning the guitar | *apprendre* |
| j'adore la lecture | zhah-dor lah lek-tewr | I love reading (la: things in general) | Grammar tables: Definite articles: the |
| j'ai souvent la flemme | zhay soo-vahN lah flem | I often can't be bothered (informal) | *avoir la flemme* |
| Je pense que | zhuh pahNs kuh | I think (that), to give an opinion | *Je pense que…* |
| Je préfère les sports d'équipe | zhuh pray-fair lay spor day-keep | I prefer team sports | *préférer* |
| quand même | kahN mem | all the same, still | *quand même* |
| Du coup | dew koo | so, as a result (informal) | *du coup* |
| Bref | bref | anyway, in short (to wrap up) | *bref* |

### Notice this: Me, te, lui: the pronoun goes before the verb

Plaire à and jouer quelque chose à take an indirect object (à + a person), and its pronoun comes before the verb: Ça te plaît ? (literally: does it please to you?). With two verbs, it goes before the infinitive it belongs to: Tu pourrais me jouer quelque chose ? Pourrais is the conditional of pouvoir, a polite could.

- **Et la guitare, ça te plaît ?** (ay lah gee-tar, sah tuh pleh) — *And the guitar, do you like it? (te = to you, before plaît)*
- **Du coup, tu pourrais me jouer quelque chose un jour ?** (dew koo, tew poo-reh muh zhoo-ay kel-kuh shohz uhN zhoor) — *So, could you play me something one day? (me before the infinitive jouer)*
- **Je lui parle.** (zhuh lwee parl) — *I'm talking to him / to her. (lui = à + one person)*

See the table: Grammar tables, Indirect object pronouns: me, lui, leur...

### Comprehension questions

1. What instrument is Bastien learning?
   a) The drums
   b) The guitar
   c) The piano
   d) The violin
2. How often does Zoé go running?
   a) Every day
   b) Once a week
   c) Three times a week
   d) Twice a week
3. What will they do on Sunday?
   a) Go running, then have a drink
   b) Go to a concert
   c) Play football, then eat out
   d) Read at the library
4. How does Bastien say he can't be bothered to do sport?
   a) J'ai souvent envie de faire du sport.
   b) J'ai souvent la flemme de faire du sport.
   c) Je fais souvent du sport après le travail.
   d) Je n'aime pas la lecture.
